Santa Elena de Uairén is a major transit point for travelers heading to the south of Venezuela. Excursions to the waterfalls and tepuis of the Gran Sabana start here. Many of the town's residents speak Portuguese, reflecting its proximity to Brazil.

## Holidays in Santa Elena de Uairén

### Santa Elena de Uairén — everything for tourists!

Until the early 1930s, this was a remote provincial town, much like many others in the country. The discovery of diamond deposits nearby changed everything, especially after the road connecting Venezuela and Brazil was completed, providing the only land road between the two countries. The town began to develop rapidly. It has almost no historic buildings or monuments, but plenty of facilities for visitors. Many modern hotels, bars, restaurants, cafés and nightclubs have been built here.

Santa Fe lies southeast of Santa Cruz. The diving program described for the island lists 2 dive sites, with a boat journey of around 1 hour from the base.

Underwater encounters here include reef fish, turtles, moray eels, sea lions and rays. Invertebrates live on the seabed and among the rocks. According to Anna's description, currents are usually calm and the water is clear, although conditions depend on the ocean on the day of the trip. Santa Fe is listed among the possible sites, and a visit is confirmed when the route is selected.

Santa Clara is the capital of Villa Clara Province. This Cuban city preserves the memory of Ernesto Che Guevara, the celebrated freedom fighter, and his historic legacy. World-famous Cuban cigars are produced at the local full-cycle tobacco factory. It is here that high-quality tobacco for "Montecristo", "Partagas" and "Romeo y Julieta", as well as "Robaina" cigars, is produced.

Leoncio Vidal Park (Parque Leoncio Vidal) is located in the center of Santa Clara and is considered the city's "heart". Reserved exclusively for pedestrians, it is always full of local residents and tourists enjoying leisurely walks.

## Santa Clara — guardian of Cuba's history!

Surrounded by green hills, the city has many architectural monuments that evoke the atmosphere of colonial-era Cuba. Many famous actors and performers have appeared on stage at the La Caridad Theatre, including Enrico Caruso, Libertad Lamarque, Jorge Negrete, Lola Flores and, of course, the Cuban National Ballet.

Santa Cruz de la Sierra, better known as Santa Cruz, is the capital of Santa Cruz Department in eastern Bolivia. The city was founded mainly by settlers from Spain and became an important staging point for Jesuits and other Christian missions in Chiquitos and Moxos over the next two centuries. In the first half of the 20th century, it began to play an important role in the country's history.

Today Santa Cruz is not only Bolivia's most populous city but also its wealthiest; it is also described as a center of drug trafficking. The city's principal attractions include September 24 Square and the cathedral located there, which now houses a museum with exhibits of religious art, the Natural History Museum, and the zoo, considered one of the best in South America.

In the first half of the 20th century, Santa Cruz began to play an important role in the country's history. Two wars contributed to this: a conflict with Brazil at the start of the 20th century and the Chaco War with Paraguay in 1930. Effectively isolated from the rest of the country, the city was only connected to Cochabamba by road in the 1950s, followed by a railway link with Brazil, stimulating its economic and population growth.

Amboró National Park lies northwest of Santa Cruz. Three ecosystems meet here: the Andean foothills, the Amazon River basin and the eastern plains. Its distinctive geographical position, landscape and diversity of flora and fauna attract tourists from around the world. Recent research has estimated the number of plant species at 638, although many species have yet to be clearly identified. Excursions are organized from Santa Cruz to Noel Kempff Mercado National Park on the Brazilian border. It is described as the only natural site designated by UNESCO as World Heritage. Noel Kempff Mercado protects five types of ecosystems — jungle, dry forest, savanna and humid forest. Santa Cruz is also known for its mild climate.
